scope: Gate comparison only; no chord/style/query enumeration, harmonic requirements, bass constraints, root requirements, deduplication or ranking membership claimed. Strict mute has no matching comparator semantics.

conventions.thumb_source: evaluateHandPlayability destructuring default is false; both generator implementations pass optional flag unchanged
conventions.S: All stopped fret crowns, including an allocated thumb if enabled; opens and omitted strings excluded
conventions.p5: monotonic OR (G <= 4 AND S <= 95); common hand gate applied separately
conventions.evaluator_role: Exact engineering comparator output, never physical ground truth

cases.expectation: Zero fretting demand control; no finger needs a string contact.
Three neighboring stops can invite one barre or separate fingertips.
Single full-width barre at a short fret-cell position tests contact geometry.
Five distinct stops stress assignment completeness and fingertip count; no human negative label.
Alternation tests whether a lower barre plus separate higher stops avoids contact conflicts.
Full-width alternation stresses contact grouping, approach, and neighboring fingers.
Four adjacent high-position stops stress narrow fret cells and fingertip collision.
Widely separated low-position stops stress longitudinal reach with lateral spread.
Only two active fingertips with substantial low-position separation test reach beyond a coarse global span bound.
Translated fret-count pattern isolates shorter high-position physical spacing from fret-count span.
Very long longitudinal separation challenges any finite-size hand geometry; no human impossibility assertion.
Outer-string endpoints test a full-width contact or distinct fingers when middle strings are merely unplayed.
Outer-string tips at neighboring frets stress palm orientation and lateral reach.
Reversed outer-string fret order tests assignment symmetry and palm-pose assumptions.
Ringing open string between same-fret stops blocks an indiscriminate barre across them.
Five adjacent stops beside ringing high E stress finite barre endpoint clearance.
Three isolated stops alternating with ringing opens stress pad widths and approach.
Omitted internal string is not required to be touched; establishes omission semantics.
Same notes as omission control, but all -1 strings require damping contact; solver must honor or declare unsupported semantics.
A damped internal string among five stops challenges uniform-pressure barre and mute-contact semantics.
Nonmonotone fret order tests alternate digit assignments and whether apparent crossing can be avoided.
Reversed zigzag stresses mirrored assignment and collision handling; crossing is a hypothesis, not prescribed fingering.

microbenchmark.limitation: Sequential warmed microbenchmark cycles fixed fixtures. Includes per-call timer overhead. Does not measure full generator search or physical accuracy.
